I've been working this land for 40 years. My field is 1.5 mu — I know every corner of it. Some of my children and grandchildren work in the city now, so it's mostly me doing the farming. At my age I keep things simple. I grow maize because I know maize. I know what it needs, I know when it's thirsty, I know when the corn borer comes.

For seed, I'll buy hybrid seed from the township supply shop — the same kind I've used for years, probably Xianyu or Zhengdan. Traditional seed doesn't yield as well anymore, and I'm not experimenting at 65.

For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and then top-dress with urea when the stalks are knee-high. That's what my neighbors do, that's what I've always done. I won't skimp — a small field still needs proper feeding.

My well gives me water when rain is short. I'll pump three times: once to help the seeds germinate if the soil is dry, once at jointing, once at silking. That's when maize is thirstiest.

I'll spray herbicide after emergence — I can't weed by hand like I used to. And one round of insecticide for the corn borer, usually mid-summer.

Rotary tillage before planting, like always. The tractor driver from the village does it for a small fee.

I expect around 500 jin per mu. A normal year.
